quality_assessment: Comprehensive and well-structured page with excellent visual aids (Mermaid diagrams). Documentation is mostly accurate but missing some advanced features like --type-clear, --glob-case-insensitive, and --ignore-file. The page effectively uses MkDocs Material features (admonitions, code annotations) and has strong visual organization.

issues.description: Missing documentation for --type-clear flag which is available in ripgrep
issues.fix_suggestion: Add documentation for --type-clear TYPE flag that clears custom type definitions. This is complementary to --type-add and allows removing built-in type definitions. Example: rg --type-clear rust --type-add 'rust:*.rs' pattern

issues.description: Type composition with include: is mentioned in features but not explained in documentation
issues.fix_suggestion: Add example showing how to use include: syntax in --type-add to compose types from other types. Example from source: '--type-add 'src:include:cpp,py,md'' allows creating a type that includes multiple existing types.

Add --glob-case-insensitive flag which makes all -g/--glob patterns case-insensitive (equivalent to using --iglob for all globs). This is useful when you have multiple glob patterns and want them all case-insensitive.
Add --ignore-file PATH flag that allows specifying additional custom ignore files beyond .gitignore and .ignore. This is useful for project-specific ignore patterns.

issues.description: Missing --no-ignore-exclude flag in granular ignore control
issues.fix_suggestion: Document --no-ignore-exclude flag which skips .git/info/exclude files. This should be added to the Granular Ignore Control section alongside --no-ignore-vcs, --no-ignore-global, etc.

issues.current_content: Files with lines longer than 200 chars are considered binary
issues.should_be: --max-columns-preview controls how many bytes to preview when detecting binary files via NUL bytes, not line length
issues.fix_suggestion: Clarify that --max-columns-preview sets the number of bytes to check for NUL characters during binary detection, not a line length threshold. The flag tunes the binary detection heuristic.
issues.source_reference: docs/binary-data/detection.md likely has more accurate explanation

issues.description: Slight ambiguity about -uu flag behavior with binary files
issues.current_content: Also search hidden files and binary files
issues.fix_suggestion: Clarify that -uu specifically adds --no-ignore and --hidden. Binary file searching is controlled separately. The current description 'Also search hidden files and binary files' might imply -uu directly enables binary searching, but that's a side effect of --no-ignore in recursive mode.
